findings.summary: The change adds a new Today ordering rule (high-priority suggestions first) but does not update screen.today, any requirement (S.webapp.prompts/S.webapp.due/S.webapp.qualification), or the bounded-prompts criterion, so the ordering and its interaction with the five-card cap are untraced and unverified.
findings.evidence: RelationshipGoal: "Suggestions for high-priority goals are listed first on Today"; screen.today: "0–5 cards ... Each card has one person label, reason..." (no ordering); C.webapp.prompts.bounded: "Six due goals yield exactly five ordered cards" (no priority case)

findings.summary: Priority changes are added to the schedule-correctness criterion even though priority does not affect due dates or qualification, so the fixture targets the wrong behavior while the actual priority effect (Today ordering) remains untested.
findings.evidence: C.webapp.schedule.correct: "Fixed-clock fixtures cover zero logs, qualification, interval, depth and priority changes..."; S.webapp.due: "dueDate must equal anchor plus intervalDays" (no priority)

findings.summary: The UI states priority defaults to normal, but the entity makes priority a required field with no default, leaving existing goals and saves that omit priority undefined.
findings.evidence: GoalPriorityField: "priority high or normal, default normal"; RelationshipGoal field: "{ name: priority, type: \"enum high|normal\" }" (optional: false, no default)
